summary: C181 ports all of dat/Tou-goal.lua:1-159 and its natural Tourist quest-goal loader. source.branch: A wizard level teleport selects the Tourist quest goal prototype Tou-goal. C makelevel dispatches the special level through makemaz and load_special, which executes dat/Tou-goal.lua; the current JavaScript registry lacks that program and throws before its first descriptor runs.
callers: nethack-c/upstream/src/wizcmds.c:wiz_level_tele (397-406) calls teleport.c:level_tele (1165); level_tele schedules the destination with do.c:schedule_goto (2057-2070). allmain.c:moveloop_core calls do.c:deferred_goto after rhack; deferred_goto calls do.c:goto_level (1479-1998), which calls mklev.c:mklev (1577), and mklev calls makelevel (1251-1446). makelevel calls mkmaze.c:makemaz (1127-1230) for this special prototype; makemaz calls sp_lev.c:load_special (6454-6503), which executes dat/Tou-goal.lua. After the loader returns, natural makelevel fills special rooms through sp_lev.c:fill_special_room -> shknam.c:stock_room -> shknam.c:shkinit.

JavaScript mirrors the production dispatch: js/wizcmds.js:wiz_level_tele -> js/teleport.js:level_tele -> js/do.js:schedule_goto -> js/allmain.js:deferred_goto -> js/do.js:deferred_goto -> goto_level -> js/mklev.js:mklev -> makelevel -> makemaz -> load_special. mklev.js:ensureSpecialLevelLoaders merges QUEST_LEVEL_LOADERS from quest_levels.js; registering Tou-goal there wires the existing natural dispatcher.

After natural load_special returns, mklev.c:makelevel fills its special rooms through sp_lev.c:fill_special_room -> shknam.c:stock_room -> shknam.c:shkinit. The matching JavaScript makelevel tail follows the same fill path. C176 accepted the complete shkinit implementation and its occupied-shopkeeper relocation evidence.
dependencies: dat/Tou-goal.lua:111-115 constructs valid trap cells with selection.area(...):filter_mapchar(".") and subtracts the two shop bounds with selection subtraction. The complete numeric l_selection_sub / selection-algebra-values port is accepted in C176 at tested commit 7288ae883c74f0469a62169bfd5eeb2e9ee69429; this task calls the existing operator without editing its contract.

Three filled barracks, one morgue and two shop regions are finalized by the existing special-room fill path. Complete shknam.c:shkinit and contract:shopkeeper-placement were accepted in C176 at the same tested commit; C181 does not edit that owner.

All descriptor names in Tou-goal.lua have existing handlers in js/mklev.js:createSpecialLevelApi, including map, region, non_diggable, stair, door, object, trap, monster and wallify. The only missing behavior on the queue path is the whole program body plus its registry entry.

The separate wizard wiz_load_splua -> load_special -> lspo_finalize_level caller can load a named des file outside natural makelevel. It is not the selected entrypoint; retain any direct-load probe separately if it still reaches the known makemon_create.js shopkeeperCall / C makemon(MM_ESHK) gate.

The first post-loader differential matched through segment 0 step 18, then diverged at step 19 when Tou-goal.lua:144-152 began creating Kops: C makemon.c:m_initweap:402-409 performs rn2(4) for a CREAM_PIE stack, then rn2(3) and rn2(2) for CLUB/RUBBER_HOSE; existing js/makemon_create.js:m_initweap omitted the S_KOP arm and entered the generic rnd(14) arm instead. The approved scope now includes the whole makemon.c:m_initweap function and js/makemon_create.js. Calls to m_initthrow and mongets discard their return values; the existing muse.c:rnd_offensive_item return-valued callee is already implemented in JS. After the S_KOP port, the natural v36/v36-quest-tou-goal replay matches all 60 recorded boundaries.

evidence: The latest saved combined queue at accepted commit 7288ae883c74f0469a62169bfd5eeb2e9ee69429 records v36/v36-quest-tou-goal at 19/60 matched screens and 19/60 matched cursors before stopping at segment 0, step 19 with unsupported level change: makelevel has no loader for special level Tou-goal. RNG matches through the boundary. The queue preserves manifest, recording and evaluation digests in .cache/C181-queue-entry.json.

Read the complete upstream dat/Tou-goal.lua at lines 1-159. Its embedded map contains 20 rows of 76 characters; the program issues 25 region descriptors, 27 fixed door descriptors, one stair, 15 object descriptors, six randomized trap placements, 38 monster descriptor calls, and wallify. Descriptor order and each loop are part of the whole Lua port.

Lines 111-115 select floor map characters, subtract the shop rectangles, then destructively choose six trap coordinates. This is the same numeric selection contract validated by C176. The 25 region calls include three filled barracks, a filled morgue and two shops; natural level generation fills these after load_special, reaching the already accepted C176 shopkeeper implementation.

The current JS registry in js/quest_levels.js has no Tou-goal key, while js/mklev.js:ensureSpecialLevelLoaders consumes that registry and throws the exact queue refusal from makelevel. The source caller path runs through the natural #wizlevelport transition. The independent #wizloaddes command goes through wiz_load_splua and is a separate diagnostic caller, not evidence for the selected natural entry.

After the whole Tou-goal loader was wired, a targeted C/JS scan exposed a second source-traced dependency at segment 0 step 19: makemon.c:m_initweap S_KOP (402-409) was absent from js/makemon_create.js, so C drew rn2(4) while JS entered the generic rnd(14) branch. C181 expanded to the complete m_initweap function under an atomic source reservation. After adding the source-ordered pie and CLUB/RUBBER_HOSE gates, node scripts/scan-sessions.mjs --json --synthetic v36/v36-quest-tou-goal reported no divergence, all 60 screens, and a matched input boundary.
